title: Camp 3 close: a day with the practices
hook: a whole day shaped by prayer, dhikr, du'a, halal and giving

segments.voice: Yesterday: a thorny branch moved off a road, the lowest branch of faith and still a branch. Your line was clear the path. Today, the whole camp in one day. Day one hundred fifty-six.

I can do this. That was the promise of this camp, back on day ninety-seven, when it began with a single word: niyyah, the intention. Mean it first. Since then you've learned the prayer one movement at a time, learned how to start again, counted glory on your fingers, watched for a new moon, broken a fast with a date, stood at Arafah in your mind, asked with open hands, walked into a mosque, looked hard at what's halal, and given in a dozen small ways. So today, no new word. Just one ordinary day, from waking to sleep, with everything in it.
screen: `IT BEGAN WITH NIYYAH.` → `ONE MOVEMENT, ONE PRACTICE AT A TIME.` → `TODAY: ONE WHOLE DAY.`

segments.voice: It starts in the dark. Eyes open, and the first words are praise for being given life again. Taharah: wudu at the sink, slowly. Then the dawn prayer, facing the qiblah. Takbir. Qiyam. Ruku'. Sujud, closest when lowest. Tashahhud, then taslim, peace to both sides. Thirty-three, thirty-three, thirty-four on the fingers. Breakfast: bismillah, something halal and good. Then the day, which is most of it. Work, done honestly. A smile at the cashier, which is sadaqah. A stone moved from the road. At midday, the sun reaches its height and the day bows again: dhuhr. In the afternoon, asr. And in between, du'a, just asking, in any language, trusting, as the Qur'an says, that He is near. At sunset, maghrib. On the way home, something for the neighbor. At night, isha, and maybe, in the last prostration, the thing you've wanted to ask all day. Then before sleep: in Your name I die and I live. The Qur'an says, in Surah an-Nisa, that the prayer is prescribed for believers at fixed times. And Bukhari reports the Prophet ﷺ asking: if there were a river at your door and you bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt be left on you? That's the shape of the day this camp has built. Not one long act of worship. Five small returns, and everything in between leaning toward them. The next camp turns from practice to the text itself: the thirtieth part of the Qur'an, the short surahs most Muslims know by heart.
screen: `DAWN: WAKE, WASH, AND BOW.` · `THE DAY: CLEAN MONEY, A SMILE, A STONE.` · `NOON TO NIGHT: FIVE RETURNS.` · `A RIVER AT YOUR DOOR.` · then, large: `A DAY THAT BOWS.`

segments.voice: Picture tomorrow's five points, dawn, noon, midafternoon, sunset and night, and at each one a small pause: if you pray, the salat; if you don't, one quiet minute and one breath of thanks. Around them, place one smile, one clean deal, one thing moved from someone's way. Hold it all lightly.
Taharah, purification: the first step of a day that wove together the prayer, dhikr, the fast, du'a, the mosque, halal and giving.
Your line: a day that bows. From niyyah to here, one movement at a time. Camp three, complete.

howItsDone: Many Muslims shape each day around the five prayers, with dhikr after them, du'a throughout, attention to halal food and earning, and small acts of charity in between.

fork.setup: there's a river at your door, and you bathe in it five times a day. the Prophet ﷺ asks: would any dirt be left on you?
options: yes, the dirt of the day stays
fork.reveal: the companions said no dirt would remain, and he said that is the likeness of the five prayers (Bukhari 528).

original.note: Arabic: the five prayers, the frame of a Muslim's day.

trapdoor: what you thought: Islamic practice is a long list of separate rules.
what it means: it's one day, shaped by five prayers, with dhikr, du'a, halal and giving in between.
what a scholar hears: kitaban mawqutan, prayer at fixed times (4:103); the river hadith (Bukhari 528, Muslim 667); niyyah first (Bukhari 1).
